## Argument

### 1. Verified inputs

ATT-0048, CLM-0048-6 constructs the canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 without a global splitting, and CLM-0048-7 gives deg(W_5)=16 at (g,n)=(6,6). ATT-0048, CLM-0048-4, CLM-0048-5 and CLM-0048-7 identify, for a base carrying six disjoint ordered sections, the Fitting locus Z_ev with the relative-triviality locus of N=omega⊗W_5^vee(Gamma), as an equality of ideals and with smooth-atlas descent. Every one of CLM-0048-1 through CLM-0048-7 is confirmed independently by REV-0091 and REV-0092. SRC-0004 supplies the convention W_f=(O(2)⊗gamma^*O(-f))|_C and deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f. C66-001-v4/FND-0105 supplies the weak CE relative-canonical normalization used fibrewise below.

### 2. Riemann–Roch and Clifford

On a geometric fibre C_b, deg(W_{5,b})=16 and deg(omega_b)=10, hence deg(L_b)=6 and chi(L_b)=6-6+1=1. Serre duality gives

h^1(L_b)=h^0(omega_b⊗L_b^{-1})=h^0(omega_b^{⊗2}⊗W_{5,b}^vee)=h^0(M_b),

so h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b). Also deg(M_b)=20-16=4 and

h^1(M_b)=h^0(omega_b⊗M_b^{-1})=h^0(L_b)≥1,

so M_b is special. Clifford's theorem gives h^0(M_b)≤4/2+1=3. Equality holds precisely when C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b≅(g^1_2)^{⊗2}; the O and omega equality cases are excluded by deg(M_b)=4.

### 3. Balanced CE normalization and the two values

On C_b the weak normalization is

O(1)|_{C_b}≅omega_{C_b/P^1}⊗gamma_b^*A_b≅omega_b⊗gamma_b^*O(2)⊗gamma_b^*A_b.

SRC-0004 gives deg(O(1)|_{C_b})=2g+6=18. The right side has degree 10+8+4deg(A_b), so deg(A_b)=0. Since Pic^0(P^1)=0, A_b≅O. Therefore

W_{5,b}≅O(1)|_{C_b}^{⊗2}⊗gamma_b^*O(-5)≅omega_b^{⊗2}⊗gamma_b^*O(-1),

and, for a fibre divisor D_b of gamma_b,

L_b≅omega_b(-D_b),  M_b≅O(D_b)=gamma_b^*O(1).

Pullback of sections along the finite surjective gamma_b is injective, hence h^0(M_b)≥h^0(P^1,O(1))=2. Together with Clifford, h^0(M_b)∈{2,3} and h^0(L_b)∈{3,4}.

### 4. The jump locus

Upper semicontinuity makes {h^0(L_b)≥4} closed. Since 3 and 4 are the only values, this is B_4 and its complement is B_3. If b∈B_4, then h^0(M_b)=3, so C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b≅2H for the hyperelliptic pencil H. Writing h:C_b->P^1 for the hyperelliptic map, one has M_b≅h^*O(2). Moreover

H^0(C_b,h^*O(2))=H^0(P^1,O(2)),

because h_*O_{C_b}=O⊕O(-7), whose second summand contributes no sections after tensoring by O(2). The morphism gamma_b is defined by a base-point-free two-dimensional subspace of this three-dimensional space, hence by a base-point-free pencil in H^0(P^1,O(2)). It therefore factors as gamma_b=q∘h for a degree-two map q:P^1->P^1. Thus gamma_b is non-primitive. The converse, and hence emptiness of B_4 under balancedness, is not proved.

### 5. Linear systems on the strata and globally

Give B_3 and B_4 their reduced locally closed structures. On B_k the value h^0(L_b)=k is constant. Grauert's theorem makes pi_*L locally free of rank k and compatible with base change there. Effective divisors whose associated line bundle is relatively L are therefore represented over B_k by P((pi_*L)^vee), with fibres |L_b|≅P^{k-1}.

Over all of B, let H=Hilb^6(C/B), which agrees with Sym^6_B(C) for a smooth relative curve. The Abel–Jacobi map H->Pic^6(C/B) and the section [L]:B->Pic^6(C/B) define

I=H×_{Pic^6(C/B)}B.

The relative Picard is separated, so I is closed. This construction remains valid when h^0 jumps and is the global degree-six linear system. No global identification with Proj(pi_*L) is made.

### 6. Scheme-theoretic link to Z_ev in the verified scope

Let H^dist⊂H be the distinct-support open and pull it back to the ordered configuration stack Conf_6(C/B). Ordering the six distinct points gives a finite étale S_6-torsor at stack level. Set tilde I=Conf_6(C/B)×_H I. Both ordered and unordered spaces retain their scheme structures; no reduction is applied to only one side.

Over Conf_6(C/B), the universal divisor is a sum of six disjoint sections, so ATT-0048 applies exactly as stated. Its CLM-0048-4, CLM-0048-5 and CLM-0048-7, confirmed by both REV-0091 and REV-0092, identify the Fitting locus Z_ev with relative triviality of omega⊗W_5^vee(Gamma). Line-bundle algebra identifies that condition with O(Gamma) relatively isomorphic to W_5⊗omega^{-1}=L. Hence Z_ev=tilde I as closed substacks, by equality of Fitting and Abel–Jacobi ideals rather than agreement of geometric points.

### 7. Separation of status

Proved here: the Riemann–Roch identity, Clifford bound and equality case, reduction to h^0∈{3,4}, semicontinuity stratification, non-primitive hyperelliptic containment of B_4, projective-bundle models on both strata, and the global Abel–Jacobi incidence construction.

Source-backed inputs: SRC-0004 for the CE sign convention and degrees; C66-001-v4/FND-0105 for the weak CE normalization; ATT-0048 with confirmations REV-0091 and REV-0092 for the canonical filtration and the scheme-theoretic Fitting comparison on ordered disjoint configurations.

Computational hypotheses: none. The degree calculations 16, 6 and 4 are reproduced symbolically; no finite experiment establishes a universal claim.

Open gaps: GAP-H0-1, namely whether B_4 is empty for balanced covers; nonemptiness of the distinct-support open on every fibre; all component, dimension, stabilizer, closure and codimension questions; and all Hodge/Tate consequences. In particular chi(L)=1 proves only that the full Abel–Jacobi fibre is nonempty, not that it contains a reduced divisor.

claims.justification: ATT-0048/CLM-0048-7 and SRC-0004 give deg W_5=16. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality give the identity and speciality; Clifford gives the bound.
claims.statement: For L=W_5⊗omega^{-1} and M=omega^{⊗2}⊗W_5^vee on every balanced genus-6 geometric fibre, deg L=6, deg M=4, chi(L)=1, and h^0(L)=1+h^0(M); M is special and h^0(M)≤3.

claims.justification: Degree comparison kills A_b∈Pic^0(P^1), the SRC-0004 negative-twist convention gives W_{5,b}≅omega_b^{⊗2}⊗gamma_b^*O(-1), pullback supplies two sections, and CLM-0066-1 supplies the upper bound.
claims.statement: Under the weak CE normalization, M_b≅gamma_b^*O(1), so h^0(M_b)∈{2,3} and h^0(L_b)∈{3,4}.

claims.justification: Upper semicontinuity and CLM-0066-2 give the two strata. Clifford equality gives M=2g^1_2; the equality H^0(C,h^*O(2))=H^0(P^1,O(2)) makes the tetragonal pencil factor through the hyperelliptic map.
claims.statement: B_4={h^0(L)=4} is closed, B_3={h^0(L)=3} is open, and B_4 lies in the hyperelliptic non-primitive locus.

claims.justification: Grauert applies after restricting to the constant-h^0 stratum; the usual divisor-of-a-section construction identifies the relative effective-divisor incidence with P((pi_*L)^vee).
claims.statement: On each reduced stratum B_k, pi_*L is locally free of rank k and base-change compatible, and the relative linear system is a P^{k-1}-bundle.

claims.justification: Hilb^6 equals Sym^6 for a smooth relative curve, and the incidence is the fibre of the Abel–Jacobi map over [L]; it is closed because Pic^6(C/B) is separated.
claims.statement: Across the jump, the correct global degree-six linear system is the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence I=Hilb^6(C/B)×_{Pic^6(C/B)}B, not an unqualified Proj(pi_*L).

claims.justification: The universal divisor there is a sum of six disjoint sections. ATT-0048/CLM-0048-4, CLM-0048-5 and CLM-0048-7, confirmed by REV-0091 and REV-0092, identify the Fitting ideal with the relative-triviality incidence ideal. Ordering distinct sections is a free finite S_6-action at stack level.
claims.statement: On the ordered distinct-support configuration stack, the pullback of I equals Z_ev scheme-theoretically and maps to the unordered distinct-support incidence as a finite étale S_6-torsor.

novelty_claims: Repairs the prior H6 import by citing the now-supplied dual-confirmed dependency package and restricting the scheme-theoretic identification to the ordered disjoint-section scope actually proved by ATT-0048.
Describes both h^0 strata uniformly: the Abel–Jacobi incidence is a P^2-bundle over B_3 and a P^3-bundle over B_4, while retaining the global Hilbert/Abel–Jacobi model across the jump.

summary: Proves the weakest scheme-correct h^0 stratification of the balanced tetragonal residual degree-six system. The only fibrewise values are 3 and 4; the corresponding Abel–Jacobi linear systems are respectively P^2- and P^3-bundles, and the h^0=4 locus is confined to non-primitive hyperelliptic covers. Globally the system is the closed Abel–Jacobi/Hilbert incidence rather than Proj(pi_*L). On the ordered distinct-support locus, and only there as required by the verified dependency's scope, it agrees scheme-theoretically with Z_ev by ATT-0048, REV-0091 and REV-0092. Emptiness of the jump stratum remains open.

theorem_scope.base: locally Noetherian over a characteristic-zero field
theorem_scope.dependency_scope: ATT-0048 is used only on the ordered pairwise-distinct configuration stack, exactly within its six-disjoint-sections and smooth-atlas descent scope
theorem_scope.exclusions: emptiness of B_4 (GAP-H0-1), reduced-support nonemptiness on every fibre, dimension or codimension in M_{6,6}, components, stabilizers, closure, smoothness, monomorphic embedding into M_{6,6}, and all Hodge/Tate conclusions
theorem_scope.generality: fibrewise balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl families with the canonical filtered quotient W_5 of ATT-0048 and the standard weak CE relative-canonical normalization

theorem_statement: Let B be a locally Noetherian scheme over a field of characteristic zero, let pi:C->B be smooth proper with geometrically connected genus-6 fibres, and let gamma:C->P^1_B be finite flat of degree 4 with fibrewise balanced Casnati–Ekedahl relations bundle F_b≅O(4)⊕O(5). Use the canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 supplied by ATT-0048, CLM-0048-6 and dual-confirmed by REV-0091 and REV-0092, where W_5 is the invertible quotient of fibrewise degree 16 under the SRC-0004 convention W_f=(O_{P(E^vee)}(2)⊗gamma^*O(-f))|_C. Put L=W_5⊗omega_{C/B}^{-1} and M=omega_{C/B}^{⊗2}⊗W_5^vee. Assume the standard weak CE normalization fibrewise: O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_{C_b}≅omega_{C_b/P^1}⊗gamma_b^*A_b for A_b∈Pic(P^1_{k(b)}). Then: (H1) on every geometric fibre, deg L=6, deg M=4, chi(L)=1, and h^0(L)=1+h^0(M); M is special and Clifford's theorem gives h^0(M)≤3. The normalization forces A_b≅O, hence W_{5,b}≅omega_{C_b}^{⊗2}(-D_b), L_b≅omega_{C_b}(-D_b), and M_b≅O_{C_b}(D_b)=gamma_b^*O(1), so h^0(L_b)∈{3,4}. (H2) On the underlying space of B, B_4={b:h^0(L_b)=4} is closed and B_3={b:h^0(L_b)=3} is its open complement. If B_k is given its reduced locally closed scheme structure, then pi_*L over B_k is locally free of rank k and commutes with base change. Moreover B_4 is contained in the locus of hyperelliptic fibres on which gamma_b is non-primitive, factoring through the hyperelliptic double cover. (H3) Let I=Hilb^6(C/B)×_{Pic^6(C/B)}B be the Abel–Jacobi incidence over the section [L]. It is closed, represents relative effective divisors Gamma with O(Gamma) relatively isomorphic to L, and satisfies I×_B B_k≅P((pi_*L|_{B_k})^vee), a P^{k-1}-bundle. Thus the degree-six linear system is a P^2-bundle over B_3 and a P^3-bundle over B_4, but need not be a projective bundle over all of B and is not globally identified with Proj(pi_*L). (H4) Let I^dist be the distinct-support open and let tilde I=Conf_6(C/B)×_{Hilb^6(C/B)}I. Then tilde I->I^dist is a finite étale S_6-torsor at stack level, with neither side reduced artificially. On Conf_6(C/B), the scheme-theoretic equality of ATT-0048, CLM-0048-4, CLM-0048-5 and CLM-0048-7, confirmed by REV-0091 and REV-0092, identifies tilde I exactly with the CE Fitting evaluation-failure locus Z_ev. No assertion is made that B_4 is empty, that I^dist is nonempty on every fibre, or that the full nonreduced Hilbert incidence outside the ordered distinct-support locus is covered by ATT-0048.
